title: Sherpa Tensing — Camp Nine: Future Continuous (B1) | Forbes English
description: Camp seven told you what will happen. Camp nine tells you what will already be happening — the thing that starts before you arrive and is still going when…

hero.lede: Camp seven told you what will happen. Camp nine tells you what will already be happening — the thing that starts before you arrive and is still going when you do. It is the tense of the appointed hour, and of asking for something without appearing to ask.

cards.head: In progress at a future moment
cards.body: It starts before the moment and is still running at it.
cards.ex: "This time tomorrow I 'll be flying over the Alps."

cards.head: Already arranged, running its course
cards.body: Nobody has to decide anything; it is simply going to be happening.
cards.ex: "I 'll be seeing her at the meeting anyway."

cards.head: Asking without asking
cards.body: The politest way in English to find out someone's plans.
cards.ex: "Will you be using the car tonight?"

cards.head: Two futures side by side
cards.body: Both in progress at the same future time.

cards.head: Guessing what is going on now
cards.body: A confident assumption about this very moment.

cards.head: Softening a plain future
cards.body: Less pushy than will do, because nobody chose it.
cards.ex: "I 'll be sending the invoice on Friday."

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: Nothing agrees with anything. Will is a modal, be stays in its base form, and only the main verb takes -ing — which makes this one of the easiest tenses in English to build and one of the hardest to know when to use.

charts.head: Three mistakes worth naming
charts.note: The form is simple, so the errors are nearly always the same three.

head: Not this
This
Why
rows: After a modal, be keeps its base form.
I will be know the answer.
State verbs take the plain future, not the continuous.
When I will be arriving, call me.
After when and if, use the present — the same rule as camp seven.

sections.label: The fork in the path
sections.title: Will do or will be doing?

charts.note: Both are true about the same future. What changes is whether you are naming the whole event or standing in the middle of it — and, more often than learners expect, how much you are asking of the other person.

head: Situation
Will be doing
Will do
rows:
In progress around a moment.
"At six I 'll be cooking."

The whole event.
"At six I 'll cook."
Nobody — it is simply the way the day runs.
Neutral. "Will you be going past the post office?"
A request. "Will you go past the post office?"

charts.example: This is why "Will you be using the car?" is polite and "Will you use the car?" sounds like an instruction: the continuous asks about the world, the simple asks about you.

sections.label: Trail markers
sections.title: Signal words
sections.example: If the time marker names a point and the action was under way before it, you are in camp nine.

sections.label: Interactive
sections.title: Now vs. what will be under way

diagram.intro: The amber spreads through future time the way camp six's yellow spreads through past time — same idea, other side of the line. panels.head: Future continuous — already under way
items: This time tomorrow I 'll be flying over the Alps.
Will you be using the car tonight?
Don't call him — he 'll be driving.

quiz.prompt: This time tomorrow I _____ over the Alps. (fly)
quiz.hint: In progress at a named future moment.
quiz.explain: The flight starts before that moment and is still going at it, so it takes will be + -ing.

quiz.hint: The polite way to ask about someone's plans.
quiz.explain: Will you be using…? asks about the world rather than making a request. "Will you use the car?" sounds like an instruction.

quiz.hint: A confident guess about this very moment.
quiz.explain: The future continuous is often used for what is almost certainly happening right now: he'll be driving.

quiz.prompt: I _____ on Friday, so send it Monday. (not / work)
quiz.explain: The negative puts not on will: won't be working. Be keeps its base form.

quiz.prompt: At three o'clock we _____ halfway up the ridge. (climb)
quiz.explain: The climb is already under way at three, so it takes the future continuous.

quiz.prompt: While you _____ the tents, I _____ supper. (pitch / cook)
quiz.hint: Two future actions side by side.
quiz.explain: After while we use a present form for the first half, and the second takes the future continuous.

quiz.hint: Careful — which verbs refuse the continuous?
quiz.explain: Know is a state verb, so it takes the plain future: I'll know. "Will be knowing" is not English.

quiz.prompt: Give me a ring when you _____ at the station. (arrive)
quiz.explain: After when, if and as soon as we use the present even about the future — the same rule as camp seven.

quiz.prompt: This time next year she _____ in Lisbon. (live)
quiz.hint: A situation running at a distant future moment.
quiz.explain: A situation already running at a point in the future takes the future continuous: will be living.
An offer or a spontaneous decision takes the plain future. The continuous would be odd here — nobody has arranged to answer a phone.
All afternoon describes a stretch the action fills, so the future continuous is the natural fit.

quiz.prompt: Where _____ you _____ while the flat is being painted? (stay)
quiz.explain: Wh- questions keep the same order: question word + will + subject + be + -ing.

quiz.prompt: I _____ her at the meeting anyway, so I'll pass it on. (see)
quiz.hint: Something already going to happen — nobody arranged it for this.
quiz.explain: "I'll be seeing her anyway" says the meeting is happening regardless of your errand. That is exactly what this tense is for.

quiz.prompt: By this time on Sunday the race _____ . (still / run)
quiz.hint: Still in progress at a future point.
quiz.explain: Still sits between will and be: will still be running.

results: Clean run. You can hear the difference between doing and already doing.
Solid progress. Worth a look back at camp seven before camp ten.
Good first attempt. The will do / will be doing fork is the part to read again.
